items.name: Collections Process
items.summary: Governs how past-due premium and fee balances are pursued from first delinquency through final escalation, ensuring receivables are recovered consistently and policyholders receive fair, predictable treatment before any adverse action.

subs.title: Aging Follow-Up Cadence
subs.description: Outstanding balances are worked on a defined schedule tied to aging buckets, with documented contact attempts at 30, 60, and 90 days past due. Collections staff record each touch in the billing system so that account history supports any subsequent action and aging reports reflect genuine collection effort.

subs.title: Dunning Letter Schedule
subs.description: A standardized sequence of dunning notices is issued at fixed intervals as a balance ages, using approved letter templates that meet state notice-content requirements. Timing and wording escalate progressively, from a courtesy reminder through formal demand, and every letter generated is retained on the account record.

subs.title: Escalation Thresholds
subs.description: Dollar-amount and aging triggers determine when an account moves to supervisory review, referral to an external collection agency, or cancellation for non-payment. Thresholds are documented and applied uniformly across lines of business, and any deviation requires manager approval recorded against the account.

items.name: Invoice Accuracy
items.summary: Sets the quality bar for premium invoices and the speed with which billing disputes are put right, so policyholders and agents can rely on statements being correct and errors being corrected without prolonged back-and-forth.

subs.title: Invoice Accuracy Above 99.5%
subs.description: Issued invoices must reflect the correct premium, fees, taxes, and payment plan at least 99.5% of the time, measured through periodic sampling against policy administration records. Results are reported monthly, and any breach of the threshold triggers a root-cause review of rating, endorsement, or billing-system feeds.

subs.title: Disputes Resolved Within 5 Business Days
subs.description: When a policyholder or producer challenges a billed amount, the dispute is investigated, corrected or explained, and closed within five business days of receipt. Adjustments such as premium reversals or fee waivers are documented with supporting rationale, and disputed amounts are suspended from collections activity while under review.

items.name: Payment Processing
items.summary: Defines how incoming premium payments are applied to policy accounts and how unmatched funds are cleared, keeping cash records current and preventing erroneous lapse or cancellation activity caused by misapplied money.

subs.title: Same-Day Cash Application Target
subs.description: Payments received through lockbox, electronic funds transfer, card, or agency sweep are posted to the correct policy account on the business day they are received. Posting timeliness is tracked daily, and any backlog carried overnight is reported to billing management with a clearance plan.

subs.title: Suspense Items Cleared Within 48 Hours
subs.description: Funds that cannot be matched to a policy at receipt are placed in suspense and researched immediately, with identification and application completed within 48 hours. Items that cannot be resolved in that window are escalated, and the suspense account is reconciled regularly so unapplied cash never masks a delinquency or distorts receivables.

items.name: BCP/DR Plans
items.summary: Establishes the department's preparedness to keep servicing policyholders through facility outages, system failures, and catastrophe events, when call volumes and claims-related service demand are typically at their highest.

subs.title: Documented Plans
subs.description: Business continuity and disaster recovery plans are maintained in writing for every critical operations and customer service function, identifying recovery time objectives, key personnel, system dependencies, and step-by-step recovery procedures. Plans are reviewed and updated whenever processes, systems, or staffing models change materially.

subs.title: Annual Testing
subs.description: Each plan is exercised at least once a year through tabletop simulations or live failover tests, including scenarios such as contact-center outages during a catastrophe event. Test results, gaps, and remediation actions are documented and tracked to closure before the next cycle.

subs.title: Alternate Site Capability
subs.description: The department maintains the ability to shift servicing work to an alternate location or to remote-work arrangements, with sufficient seats, telephony routing, and system access to sustain critical policyholder service levels. Capacity assumptions are validated as part of annual testing.

subs.title: Communication Protocols
subs.description: Predefined call trees and notification procedures cover employees, leadership, regulators, vendors, and distribution partners during a disruption. Protocols specify who declares an event, how policyholders are informed of service impacts, and how status updates are issued until normal operations resume.

items.name: Complaint Handling
items.summary: Governs the intake, acknowledgment, and resolution of policyholder complaints so every grievance is captured in a complete record that satisfies state market-conduct expectations and surfaces service problems early.

subs.title: Complaint Logged Within 24 Hours
subs.description: Every complaint, whether received by phone, mail, email, or through a department of insurance, is entered into the complaint register within 24 hours of receipt. The log captures the complainant, policy, line of business, nature of the grievance, and receipt channel, providing the data foundation for regulatory complaint reporting.

subs.title: Acknowledgment Sent
subs.description: The complainant receives a written or verbal acknowledgment confirming the complaint was received, who owns it, and the expected response timeframe. Acknowledgments for regulator-forwarded complaints follow the specific deadlines set by the originating state insurance department.

subs.title: Resolution Tracked
subs.description: Each complaint is tracked through to closure with its investigation findings, the response provided, and any corrective action recorded. Aging open complaints are reviewed by management, and closed-complaint data is trended by cause and business area to identify systemic service issues.

items.name: Escalation Process
items.summary: Defines when and how a complaint or service issue moves beyond the front line, ensuring serious matters reach the right level of management quickly and are resolved by people with genuine authority to act.

subs.title: Escalation Criteria Defined
subs.description: Written criteria specify which matters must be escalated, including regulator involvement, threatened litigation, allegations of agent misconduct, repeat complaints, and issues exceeding defined dollar thresholds. Front-line staff are trained on the criteria so escalation decisions do not depend on individual judgment alone.

subs.title: Management Notification
subs.description: Escalated items are routed to the designated management tier within a set timeframe, with department of insurance complaints and potential legal matters also flagged to compliance or legal counsel. Notifications include a summary of the issue, actions taken to date, and the response deadline.

subs.title: Resolution Authority
subs.description: Each escalation level carries documented authority limits for remedies such as fee waivers, premium adjustments, goodwill payments, and policy reinstatements. Decisions made under that authority are recorded with rationale, and matters exceeding a level's limits move upward rather than being settled out of grade.

items.name: Document Management
items.summary: Controls the full lifecycle of policy files, correspondence, and service records from capture through destruction, so the carrier can produce complete documentation on demand for service, audit, litigation, and market-conduct examinations.

subs.title: Indexing Standards
subs.description: Incoming and generated documents are classified and indexed against a standard taxonomy, with required metadata such as policy number, document type, line of business, and receipt date applied at capture. Indexing accuracy is sampled periodically because misfiled documents undermine both service and discovery obligations.

subs.title: Retention Schedules
subs.description: Records are kept for the periods required by the corporate retention schedule and applicable state insurance regulations, which vary by record type and jurisdiction. Legal holds suspend normal retention for affected records, and the schedule itself is reviewed against regulatory change.

subs.title: Retrieval SLA
subs.description: Indexed documents must be retrievable within a defined service level, with same-day or faster turnaround for active service requests, claims support, and regulator demands. Retrieval performance is measured, and failures are analyzed for indexing or storage-system root causes.

subs.title: Destruction Protocols
subs.description: Records that have passed their retention period and carry no legal hold are destroyed through approved secure methods, with certificates of destruction retained for physical media and verified deletion for electronic records. Destruction events are logged and approved before execution, never performed ad hoc.

items.name: Continuous Improvement
items.summary: Establishes a structured discipline for finding and removing waste in servicing operations, ensuring improvement activity is deliberate, visible, and judged by measured results rather than anecdote.

subs.title: Kaizen and Lean Initiatives
subs.description: The department runs structured improvement events using Lean and Kaizen methods, targeting high-volume servicing processes such as endorsements, billing inquiries, and correspondence handling. Events follow a defined charter, involve the staff who perform the work, and conclude with implemented changes rather than recommendations alone.

subs.title: Improvement Ideas Tracked
subs.description: Suggestions from employees, quality reviews, and complaint trends are captured in a single improvement backlog with an owner, status, and disposition for each idea. The backlog is reviewed on a regular cadence so submissions are visibly actioned or closed with feedback to the contributor.

subs.title: Benefits Measured
subs.description: Every implemented improvement is evaluated against a pre-stated baseline, quantifying gains in cycle time, cost, quality, or customer satisfaction. Realized benefits are validated after a settling period and reported to leadership, distinguishing projected savings from results actually achieved.

items.name: Process Documentation
items.summary: Requires that the department's core servicing processes are formally mapped, owned, and measurable, giving leadership an accurate picture of how work actually flows and a stable basis for training, controls, and improvement.

subs.title: Process Maps Maintained
subs.description: Current-state maps exist for each key operational process, showing steps, handoffs, systems touched, and decision points from intake to completion. Maps are refreshed whenever a process or supporting system changes, so documentation never drifts from how work is genuinely performed.

subs.title: RACI Defined
subs.description: Each documented process carries a RACI matrix assigning who is responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed for every major step, including handoffs to underwriting, claims, and IT. Accountability gaps and overlaps surfaced by the matrix are resolved by process owners rather than left ambiguous.

subs.title: Metrics Identified
subs.description: Every mapped process has defined performance measures covering volume, cycle time, quality, and cost, with stated data sources and calculation methods. These metrics feed the department's operational reporting and provide the baseline against which improvement work is judged.

items.name: Standard Operating Procedures
items.summary: Ensures that the detailed work instructions behind policy servicing are written down, kept current, and controlled, so transactions are handled the same correct way regardless of who performs them or where.

subs.title: SOPs for All Key Processes
subs.description: Step-level written procedures exist for every key process, including policy changes, billing transactions, document handling, and complaint intake, detailing system steps, state-specific variations, and exception handling. New or changed processes may not go live without an approved SOP in place.

subs.title: Annual Review Cycle
subs.description: Each SOP is reviewed at least annually by its designated owner to confirm it still reflects current systems, regulations, and practice, with off-cycle updates required when a material change occurs sooner. Review completion is tracked, and overdue procedures are escalated to department management.

subs.title: Version Control
subs.description: SOPs are held in a controlled repository where each revision carries a version number, effective date, change summary, and approver. Superseded versions are archived rather than deleted, allowing the department to demonstrate which procedure was in force at any point in time during an audit or examination.

items.name: Call Quality Monitoring
items.summary: Establishes routine evaluation of recorded customer interactions so service accuracy, compliance with required disclosures, and professionalism are verified continuously and agent development is grounded in observed behavior.

subs.title: Five Calls per Agent per Month Monitored
subs.description: Quality analysts or supervisors evaluate a minimum of five recorded or live calls for every agent each month, drawn across call types and times of day rather than cherry-picked. Monitoring volume is tracked, and shortfalls for any agent are made up in the following period.

subs.title: Quality Scorecard
subs.description: Each monitored call is scored against a standardized scorecard covering accuracy of information given, adherence to required disclosures and verification procedures, system documentation, and customer experience behaviors. Scorecard criteria are calibrated regularly among evaluators so scoring stays consistent across the team.

subs.title: Coaching Documented
subs.description: Evaluation results are reviewed with each agent in documented coaching sessions that record strengths, specific gaps, and agreed actions. Repeated failures on compliance-critical elements, such as missed disclosures or privacy verification, trigger formal performance follow-up rather than coaching alone.

items.name: Customer Satisfaction
items.summary: Defines how the department listens to policyholders and acts on what it hears, turning survey signals into concrete service fixes so satisfaction and retention are managed rather than merely observed.

subs.title: Post-Interaction Surveys
subs.description: Customers are invited to rate their experience shortly after service interactions across phone, email, chat, and policy-change transactions. Survey design, sampling, and channel coverage are governed so results are representative, and response data flows back to teams at the agent and queue level.

subs.title: NPS Tracking
subs.description: Net Promoter Score is measured on a defined cadence for both transactional touchpoints and the broader relationship, segmented by line of business and service channel. Scores are trended against targets and prior periods, and material movements prompt investigation rather than passive reporting.

subs.title: Verbatim Analysis
subs.description: Free-text survey comments are systematically categorized by theme, such as billing confusion, claim status frustration, or hold times, using consistent coding so themes can be quantified. Recurring verbatim themes are matched against complaint and quality data to confirm whether they reflect genuine process defects.

subs.title: Closed-Loop Feedback
subs.description: Detractor responses and serious dissatisfaction signals trigger outreach to the customer within a defined window to resolve the underlying issue. Outcomes of that outreach, along with systemic fixes driven by survey insight, are tracked to completion and reported so the loop demonstrably closes.

items.name: Transaction Quality
items.summary: Provides the quality assurance regime for processed servicing work such as endorsements, billing changes, and correspondence, so processing defects are detected through sampling and eliminated at the source before they reach policyholders at scale.

subs.title: Five Percent Sample Reviewed
subs.description: At least five percent of completed transactions in each work type are independently re-checked by quality reviewers against source documents and system entries. Samples are selected randomly within each processor and transaction category so results fairly represent the whole population of work.

subs.title: Accuracy Targets Above 99%
subs.description: Reviewed transactions must meet or exceed 99% accuracy, with critical defects, such as wrong coverage amounts, incorrect effective dates, or misapplied payments, weighted more heavily than cosmetic errors. Teams or individuals falling below target operate under documented remediation plans until performance recovers.

subs.title: Errors Tracked and Trended
subs.description: Every defect found in review is logged with its type, root cause, responsible process, and correction status, and identified errors are fixed on the affected policy, not just counted. Error data is trended monthly to expose patterns by transaction type, processor, or system, feeding targeted training and process changes.

items.name: Operational Reporting
items.summary: Defines the layered reporting rhythm through which servicing performance is made visible, ensuring leaders at every level work from the same numbers and that emerging problems surface in days rather than quarters.

subs.title: Daily Dashboard
subs.description: An operational dashboard is published each business day showing intake volumes, service levels, backlog and inventory aging, and staffing against plan for the contact center and processing teams. Supervisors use it to rebalance work and flag same-day risks to service commitments.

subs.title: Weekly Scorecard
subs.description: A weekly scorecard rolls daily results into performance against SLA, quality, and productivity targets, with red, amber, and green status against each goal. Misses carry a brief owner commentary explaining cause and corrective action rather than appearing as unexplained numbers.

subs.title: Monthly Business Review
subs.description: Department leadership conducts a monthly review covering full operational performance, complaint and satisfaction results, vendor performance, expense position, and progress on improvement initiatives. Decisions and action items from the review are minuted and tracked through to the following session.

subs.title: Trend Analysis
subs.description: Key operational measures are analyzed over rolling multi-month horizons to distinguish seasonal patterns, such as renewal-driven call peaks or catastrophe surges, from genuine performance shifts. Trend findings inform staffing forecasts, capacity planning, and the prioritization of improvement work.

items.name: Email/Chat SLA
items.summary: Sets the responsiveness and resolution expectations for written and digital service channels, so policyholders who choose email or chat receive service comparable in speed and completeness to a phone call.

subs.title: Email Response Within 4 Hours
subs.description: Customer and producer emails receive a substantive reply within four business hours of receipt, not merely an automated acknowledgment. Response timeliness is measured from arrival in the service queue, and aging items are escalated before the window expires.

subs.title: Chat Wait Time Under 2 Minutes
subs.description: Customers initiating a chat session are connected to a live agent in less than two minutes on average, with concurrency limits set so agents handling multiple chats can still respond promptly within each session. Wait-time performance is monitored in real time and staffing is adjusted intraday when queues build.

subs.title: First Contact Resolution Above 70%
subs.description: More than 70% of email and chat inquiries are resolved in the initial interaction without transfer, callback, or repeat contact on the same issue. Resolution is verified through repeat-contact tracking and survey confirmation, and inquiry types that routinely fail first-contact handling are targeted for knowledge-base or process fixes.

items.name: Phone SLA
items.summary: Defines the accessibility and efficiency targets for the carrier's voice channel, the primary route policyholders use for billing questions, policy changes, and claims-related service, balancing speed of answer against quality of handling.

subs.title: 80% of Calls Answered in 30 Seconds
subs.description: The contact center maintains a grade of service in which at least 80% of inbound calls reach a live agent within 30 seconds of entering the queue. Performance is measured at interval level throughout the day, not just as a daily average, so peak-period failures cannot hide inside aggregate numbers.

subs.title: Abandonment Rate Below 5%
subs.description: Fewer than 5% of queued callers may hang up before reaching an agent, measured net of very short abandons. Sustained breaches trigger review of staffing, IVR routing, and queue messaging, since abandoned calls frequently resurface as complaints or lost retention.

subs.title: Average Handle Time Targets by Call Type
subs.description: Handle-time expectations are set separately for each call category, recognizing that a billing inquiry, a policy endorsement, and a first notice of loss demand different durations. Targets are derived from observed performance of competent handling rather than imposed arbitrarily, and they are managed as a balance against quality and first-call resolution, never at their expense.

items.name: Policy Service SLA
items.summary: Establishes turnaround commitments for core policy servicing transactions, ensuring policyholders, agents, and certificate holders receive timely documents and that time-sensitive regulatory obligations around policy termination are met without exception.

subs.title: Endorsements Within 48 Hours
subs.description: Requested policy changes, such as added vehicles, coverage adjustments, or address updates, are processed and issued within 48 hours of receiving a complete request. Endorsements needing underwriting referral are flagged and tracked separately so the standard turnaround is preserved for routine changes.

subs.title: Certificates Same Day
subs.description: Certificates of insurance requested by insureds, agents, or third parties such as lenders and contract counterparties are produced and delivered the same business day. Certificate content is generated from current policy data to guarantee evidence of coverage is accurate at issuance.

subs.title: Cancellations per State Requirements
subs.description: Policy cancellations and nonrenewals are executed in strict accordance with each state's notice periods, permissible grounds, delivery methods, and proof-of-mailing requirements, which override any internal turnaround target. Compliance is verified through quality sampling, since a defective cancellation can leave the carrier on risk or expose it to regulatory action.

items.name: New Hire Training
items.summary: Governs how new operations and customer service employees are brought to full competence before handling live policyholder work independently, protecting service quality and compliance during the period when error risk is highest.

subs.title: Role-Specific Curriculum
subs.description: Each role follows a defined training curriculum covering the products and lines of business it will service, core systems, state-specific servicing rules, privacy and disclosure requirements, and the procedures for its transaction types. Curricula are maintained alongside SOPs so training content reflects current practice.

subs.title: Competency Assessments
subs.description: Trainees must pass knowledge checks and practical evaluations, such as graded simulated calls or test transactions, before progressing through and graduating from training. Assessment results are recorded, and individuals who do not meet the standard receive remediation or extended training rather than early release to production work.

subs.title: Nesting Period
subs.description: Following classroom training, new hires work live volume in a supervised nesting environment with reduced workload expectations, immediate access to coaches, and heightened quality monitoring. Graduation from nesting depends on meeting defined quality and proficiency gates, not simply on elapsed time.

items.name: Ongoing Training
items.summary: Ensures tenured servicing staff stay current as the business changes around them, sustaining accurate customer guidance and regulatory compliance long after initial onboarding ends.

subs.title: Product Updates
subs.description: Staff receive timely training whenever products, coverage forms, rates, or rules change across the carrier's P&C, life and retirement, and group benefits lines. Training is delivered before the change takes effect in the market, so agents never field customer questions about products they have not been briefed on.

subs.title: System Changes
subs.description: Releases affecting the policy administration, billing, telephony, or document systems are accompanied by training and updated job aids delivered ahead of go-live. Post-implementation support is provided during the adoption period, and recurring user errors after a release feed back into supplemental training.

subs.title: Soft Skills
subs.description: Periodic development sessions address communication, empathy, de-escalation, and handling of difficult or vulnerable customers, with content informed by call quality findings and complaint themes. These skills are reinforced through coaching rather than treated as one-time classroom events.

subs.title: Compliance Refreshers
subs.description: All servicing staff complete recurring training on privacy and information security, unfair trade practices, complaint identification, anti-fraud awareness, and other regulatory obligations on at least an annual cycle. Completion is tracked to the individual, and overdue refreshers are escalated because evidence of training is routinely requested in market-conduct examinations.

items.name: BPO Management
items.summary: Sets the control framework for business process outsourcing partners performing servicing work on the carrier's behalf, ensuring outsourced operations meet the same service, quality, and compliance standards as internal teams and that accountability never transfers with the work.

subs.title: SLAs Defined
subs.description: Every BPO engagement operates under contractual service level agreements covering turnaround times, quality and accuracy thresholds, availability, and data-handling obligations, with remedies or credits specified for misses. SLAs mirror the standards applied to equivalent in-house work so customers experience no difference by sourcing model.

subs.title: Performance Monitoring
subs.description: Vendor output is measured continuously against the contracted SLAs through vendor-submitted reporting validated by independent carrier-side sampling of completed work. Persistent underperformance triggers formal corrective action plans with defined cure periods and consequences.

subs.title: Governance Meetings
subs.description: A structured governance cadence pairs regular operational reviews of volumes, performance, and issues with periodic executive sessions covering the relationship, commercial matters, and strategic direction. Meetings produce minuted decisions and action logs that are tracked between sessions.

subs.title: Audit Rights
subs.description: Contracts reserve the carrier's right to audit vendor operations, controls, security, and records, including on-site inspection and regulator access, consistent with insurance outsourcing expectations. Audit rights are actually exercised on a risk-based schedule, and findings are remediated under tracked plans rather than noted and shelved.

items.name: Staffing Standards
items.summary: Defines the structural staffing requirements that keep servicing operations resilient, so the department can absorb absence, attrition, and volume swings without single points of failure or degraded policyholder service.

subs.title: Staffing Ratios
subs.description: Documented ratios govern staffing relative to workload drivers, including agents per supervisor, quality reviewers per production team, and headcount per forecast volume by function. Ratios are reviewed against service and quality outcomes and adjusted through the planning cycle rather than eroded silently through unfilled vacancies.

subs.title: Cross-Training Requirements
subs.description: A defined share of staff in each function must be trained and kept proficient in at least one additional work type, with skill currency maintained through periodic refreshers and rotational live work. The resulting skill matrix is documented so leaders know exactly who can flex where when volumes shift.

subs.title: Backup Coverage Plans
subs.description: Every critical function and key-person dependency has a named backup arrangement, ensuring time-sensitive work such as cancellations, regulatory correspondence, and cash application continues through vacancies, leave, and surge events. Coverage plans are tested in practice, not maintained as paper designations.

items.name: Workforce Management
items.summary: Governs the forecasting, scheduling, and intraday control disciplines that align staffing with demand, so service levels are achieved through planning rather than through chronic overtime or overstaffing.

subs.title: Forecast Accuracy
subs.description: Contact and transaction volumes are forecast at interval, daily, and seasonal horizons, incorporating drivers such as renewal cycles, billing runs, and catastrophe activity. Forecast accuracy is measured against actuals with defined variance tolerances, and persistent misses drive recalibration of the forecasting model.

subs.title: Schedule Adherence
subs.description: Agents are expected to work their published schedules within a defined adherence threshold, with conformance tracked through the workforce management system. Adherence results are reviewed in coaching, recognizing that even fully staffed days fail service levels when staff are off-plan at the interval level.

subs.title: Real-Time Management
subs.description: Dedicated real-time monitoring watches queues, occupancy, and adherence throughout the day, triggering intraday actions such as skill reassignment, break adjustments, or deferral of offline work when service levels are threatened. Intraday decisions and their outcomes are logged to improve future response playbooks.

subs.title: Overtime Approval
subs.description: Overtime is authorized in advance by designated approvers against documented business justification, rather than self-initiated by staff or used as a standing fix for understaffing. Overtime spend is tracked against budget and analyzed by cause, with recurring patterns redirected into the staffing plan.
